title: Lumina Inference Engine
description: Distributed GPU-accelerated inference gateway for custom LLMs with real-time semantic caching.

caseStudy.summary: A low-latency inference gateway design for serving custom language models without losing control of cost, quality, and observability.
caseStudy.challenge: Agentic systems can create bursty, repeated model calls. The useful layer is not just faster GPUs; it is a gateway that can cache, route, evaluate, and explain inference decisions.
approach: Separated the Python orchestration layer from Rust hot paths for request normalization, cache checks, and streaming response control.
Used semantic caching to reuse high-confidence responses while keeping cache misses observable for evaluation.
Treated every model call as an auditable event with latency, cost, prompt family, and downstream workflow context.
outcome: Reduced redundant inference work in repeatable agent flows.
Created a stronger operational boundary between prototypes and production AI services.
Made governance measurable through logs, routing policy, and failure-mode analysis.

title: Echo Spatial Engine
description: Geospatial data processor for tracking autonomous delivery drones with sub-millisecond latency.

caseStudy.summary: A streaming geospatial engine for turning fast-moving location events into operational state.
caseStudy.challenge: Crisis, logistics, and robotics workflows all need location data that is both current and explainable. A map without temporal context becomes decoration.
approach: Used Kafka topics to separate ingestion, enrichment, and alerting.
Used PostGIS for durable spatial queries and historical reconstruction.
Modeled every event as part of a time-aware operational graph.
outcome: Supported real-time tracking while keeping old states queryable.
Connected geospatial intelligence patterns to cellular and biological atlas thinking.
Made field-facing dashboards more useful by preserving provenance.

title: Melodify
description: Hackathon-winning project that scrapes a website and composes music from its content using browser-side math functions.

caseStudy.summary: A creative coding experiment that turns the visible web into a playable composition.
caseStudy.challenge: Most web analysis tools turn pages into scores, tables, or audits. Melodify asks what happens if a website becomes a performance surface instead.
approach: Extracted page content and structure, then mapped textual and visual signals into musical parameters.
Kept composition logic in the browser so the experience feels immediate.
Framed the page as an instrument rather than a document.
outcome: Connected web scraping, generative art, and interactive composition.
Created a memorable demo surface for hackathon storytelling.
Informed later thinking about projection mapping and public computation.

title: Buzzo
description: A cross-platform app for connecting fans with creators while supporting fairer payment for content and merchandise.

caseStudy.summary: A creator-community marketplace prototype focused on fan access, content ownership, and monetization.
caseStudy.challenge: Creators often have fragmented relationships with audiences across platforms, payments, and merchandise. The product needed one simple interaction model.
approach: Mapped creator, fan, content, and purchase flows into a cross-platform interface.
Prioritized lightweight account flows over a heavy marketplace backend.
Designed around direct creator-audience engagement instead of feed discovery.
outcome: Clarified the product mechanics behind creator monetization.
Created a reusable pattern for small social commerce prototypes.
Strengthened the portfolio link between product thinking and systems thinking.

title: SmartVille
description: A dashboard that works with IoT devices to modernize city-wide waste management.

caseStudy.summary: A civic operations dashboard for coordinating IoT waste signals, routing, and city service decisions.
caseStudy.challenge: Waste management is a field problem before it is a dashboard problem. Sensors only help when teams can turn readings into route, staffing, and maintenance decisions.
approach: Connected device readings to a dashboard organized around bins, locations, and urgency.
Used operational status views instead of vanity analytics.
Framed the prototype around city teams that need quick triage.
outcome: Showed how civic IoT data can support field operations.
Created a concrete example of geospatial intelligence for public services.
Gave the project a natural link to agentic workflows that act with local context.

title: Jember
description: An LMS assistant for tracking remote-class assignments and composing research excerpts.

caseStudy.summary: A remote-learning assistant for assignment memory, research support, and study continuity.
caseStudy.challenge: Remote learners lose context across calendars, LMS tools, notes, and research tabs. The missing feature is often continuity, not more content.
approach: Built around reminders, submission tracking, and excerpt composition.
Kept the workflow student-centered instead of institution-centered.
Used automation to reduce forgetfulness without replacing student judgment.
outcome: Turned scattered learning tasks into one practical workflow.
Linked education technology to agentic memory and handoff design.
Created a reusable pattern for task-aware assistants.

title: BandMetro
description: A mobile app that synchronizes a band's timing like a metronome over an ad-hoc network.

caseStudy.summary: A timing coordination prototype for musicians who need shared rhythm without centralized hardware.
caseStudy.challenge: Group performance depends on shared timing, but rehearsal contexts are messy: phones, latency, local networks, and human feel all matter.
approach: Modeled synchronization as a lightweight local coordination problem.
Designed the interface around beat visibility and fast correction.
Kept the system small enough for hackathon-scale mobile experimentation.
outcome: Connected real-time systems thinking with performance and art.
Showed how local context changes the shape of technical correctness.
Informed later work on public computation and spatial interfaces.

title: DefHacks-Learn
description: A learning site for students in the DefHacks network beginning entry-level computer science.

caseStudy.summary: A community learning surface for helping new developers find approachable entry points into computer science.
caseStudy.challenge: Beginner education is often blocked by confidence and navigation. Students need pathways, not only links.
approach: Organized starter material around approachable CS concepts.
Kept the interface lightweight so contributors could extend it.
Built from the perspective of hackathon community onboarding.
outcome: Supported a stronger bridge from community events to lasting learning.
Added an education-focused thread to the project portfolio.
Reinforced the SEO story around mentorship, open source, and technical community.
